source_text: Ἐξ ὧν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν τῷ Εὐαγγελίῳ οὕτω νοοῦν τες, τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν περὶ τῆς σαρκώσεως καὶ ἐνανθρωπήσεως τοῦ Λόγου διεβεβαιώσαντο. Τούτων τοίνυν οὕτως ὁμολογηθέντων, παρακα λοῦμεν ὑμᾶς τοὺς μὲν οὕτως ὁμολογοῦντας καὶ ἑρμη νεύοντας οὕτω τὰς λέξεις, ἃς λέγουσι, μὴ κατα κρίνετε προπετῶς, μηδὲ ἀποβάλλετε, ἀλλὰ μᾶλ λον εἰρηνεύοντας καὶ ἀπολογουμένους προσλαμβάνε σθε· τοὺς δὲ μὴ βουλομένους οὕτως ὁμολογεῖν καὶ διερμηνεύειν τὰς λέξεις, τούτους κωλύετε καὶ ἐντρέπετε, ὡς ὑπόπτους τῷ φρονήματι. Τούτων τε μὴ ἀνεχόμενοι συμβουλεύετε κἀκείνοις τοῖς ὀρθῶς ἑρμηνεύουσί τε καὶ φρονοῦσι μηδὲν πλέον ἀλλήλους ἀνα κρίνειν μηδὲ λογομαχεῖν ἐπ' οὐδὲν χρήσιμον, μήτε ταῖς τοιαύταις λέξεσι διαμάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ τῷ φρονή ματι τῆς εὐσεβείας συμφωνεῖν. Οἱ γὰρ μὴ οὕτω διανοούμενοι, ἀλλὰ μόνον ἐπὶ τοῖς τοιούτοις λεξειδίοις φιλονεικοῦντες, καὶ παρὰ τὰ ἐν Νικαίᾳ γραφέντα ζητοῦντες, οὐδὲν ἕτερον ποιοῦσιν, ἢ «ποτίζουσιν ἀνα τροπὴν θολερὰν τὸν πλησίον,» ὡς φθονοῦντες τὴν εἰρήνην καὶ ἀγαπῶντες τὰ σχίσματα. Ἀλλ' ὑμεῖς, ὡς ἀγαθοὶ ἄνθρωποι καὶ πιστοὶ δοῦλοι, καὶ οἰκονόμοι τοῦ Κυρίου, τὰ μὲν σκανδαλίζοντα καὶ ξενίζοντα παύετε καὶ κωλύετε, πάντων δὲ μᾶλλον προκρίνετε τὴν τοιαύτην εἰρήνην, οὔσης ὑγιαινούσης πίστεως· ἴσως ὁ Κύριος ἐλεήσει ἡμᾶς, καὶ συνάψει τὰ διῃρημένα, καὶ γενομένης μιᾶς ποίμνης, πάλιν πάντες ἕνα ἔχομεν καθηγεμόνα, τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν. Ταῦτα ἡμεῖς μὲν, εἰ καὶ μηδὲν πλέον ἔδει ζητεῖν τῆς ἐν Νικαίᾳ συνόδου, μηδὲ ἀνέχεσθαι τῶν ἐκ φιλονεικίας ῥημάτων, ἀλλά γε διὰ τὴν εἰρήνην, καὶ ἕνεκα τοῦ μὴ ἀποβάλλειν τοὺς ὀρθῶς πιστεύειν ἐθέλοντας, ἀνεκρίναμεν, καὶ ἅπερ ὡμολόγησαν, συντόμως ὑπηγορεύσαμεν, οἱ περιλειφθέντες ἐν τῇ Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ, κοινῇ μετὰ τῶν συλλειτουργῶν ἡμῶν Ἀστερίου καὶ Εὐσεβίου· οἱ γὰρ πλεῖστοι ἐξ ἡμῶν ἀπεδήμησαν εἰς τὰς παροικίας ἑαυτῶν. Ὑμεῖς δὲ πάλιν κοινῇ ἔνθα καὶ εἰώθατε συνάγεσθαι, ἀνάγνωτε ταῦτα, κἀκεῖ πάντας προσκαλέσασθαι καταξιώσατε. Δίκαιον γὰρ ἐκεῖ πρῶτον τὴν ἐπιστολὴν ἀναγνωσθῆναι, κἀκεῖ τοὺς βουλομένους καὶ ἀντιποιουμένους τῆς εἰρήνης συνάπτεσθαι· καὶ λοιπὸν συναφθέντων αὐτῶν, ἔνθα ἂν ἀρέσῃ πᾶσι τοῖς λαοῖς, παρούσης τῆς ὑμετέρας χρηστότητος, ἐκεῖ τὰς συνάξεις ἐπιτελεῖσθαι, καὶ τὸν Κύριον κοινῇ παρὰ πάντων δοξάζεσθαι. Προσαγορεύουσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ ἀδελφοί. Ἐῤῥῶσθαι ὑμᾶς, καὶ μνημονεύειν ἡμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ εὔχομαι, Ἐγώ τε Ἀθανάσιος· ὁμοίως τε οἱ ἄλλοι ἐπίσκοποι οἱ συνελθόντες ὑπέγραψαν· καὶ οἱ ἀποσταλέντες δὲ παρὰ μὲν Λουκίφερος τοῦ ἐπισκόπου Σαρδίας νήσου, διάκονοι δύο, Ἑρέννιος, καὶ Ἀγαπητός· παρὰ δὲ Παυλίνου Μάξιμος καὶ Καλήμερος, καὶ αὐτοὶ διάκονοι. Παρῆσαν δὲ καί τινες Ἀπολλιναρίου τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μονάζοντες, παρ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τοῦτο πεμφθέντες. Ἔστι δὲ ἕκαστος τῶν προκειμένων ἐπισκόπων, πρὸς οὓς ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἐγράφη, Εὐσέβιος πόλεως Βιργίλλων τῆς Γαλλίας, Λουκίφερ τῆς Σαρδίας νήσου, Ἀστέριος Πετρῶν τῆς Ἀραβίας, Κυμάτιος Παλτοῦ Κοίλης Συρίας, Ἀνατόλιος Εὐβοίας. Οἱ δὲ ἐπιστείλαντες ὅ τε πάπας Ἀθανάσιος, καὶ οἱ παρατυχόντες σὺν αὐτῷ ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ, αὐτός τε Εὐσέβιος καὶ Ἀστέριος· καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Γάϊος Παρατονίου τῆς ἔγγιστα Λιβύης, Ἀγαθὸς Φραγώνεως καὶ μέρους Ἐλεαρχίας τῆς Αἰγύπτου· Ἀμμώνιος Παχνεμούνεως καὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ μέρους τῆς Ἐλεαρχίας, Ἀγαθοδαίμων Σχεδίας καὶ Μενελαΐτου· Δρακόντιος Ἑρμουπόλεως μικρᾶς, Ἀδέλφιος Ὀνούφεως τῆς Λύχνων, Ἑρμίων Τάνεως, Μάρκος Ζύγρων τῆς ἔγγιστα Λιβύης, Θεόδωρος Ἀθρίβεως, Ἀνδρέας Ἀρσενοΐτου, Παφνούτιος Σάεως, Μάρκος Φίλων, Ζώϊλος Ἄνδρω, Μῆνας Ἀντίφρων.
thought_title: Counsel for peace and the letter's closing
orientation: Athanasius and the bishops with him are concluding their letter to the Antiochene leaders, urging them to receive those who confess rightly and to end quarrels over words.
pass_a_gloss: From which things also all the things in the Gospel, understanding them thus, they affirmed to think the same thing about the incarnation and the becoming human of the Word. These things therefore having been confessed thus, we urge you: those who confess thus and interpret thus the words which they speak, do not condemn rashly, nor reject, but rather receive them as making peace and making a defense. But those who are not willing to confess thus and to interpret the words, these hinder and shame, as suspect in their thinking. And not tolerating these, counsel also those who interpret rightly and think rightly to examine one another nothing further nor to quarrel over words for nothing useful, nor to fight about such words, but to agree in the thinking of piety. For those who do not think thus, but only contend about such little words, and seek beyond the things written in Nicaea, do nothing other than 'give a neighbor a turbid overthrow to drink,' as envying peace and loving divisions. But you, as good men and faithful servants and stewards of the Lord, stop and hinder the things that cause scandal and astonish, and prefer above all things such peace, since the faith is sound. Perhaps the Lord will have mercy on us, and will join the divided things, and when there is one flock, again we all have one leader, our Lord Jesus Christ. These things we, even if nothing further was necessary to seek beyond the council in Nicaea, nor to tolerate the words from love of strife, yet for the sake of peace, and for the sake of not rejecting those who wish to believe rightly, examined, and what things they confessed, we briefly dictated, those remaining in Alexandria, in common with our fellow ministers Asterius and Eusebius; for the majority of us were away to their own districts. But you again in common, where also you are accustomed to gather, read these things, and there deem worthy to summon all. For it is right that there first the letter be read, and there those who wish and claim peace be joined. And for the rest, when they have been joined, wherever it pleases all the peoples, your kindness being present, there let the assemblies be performed, and let the Lord be glorified in common by all. The brothers with me greet you. I pray that you be strong and remember us in the Lord. I myself Athanasius; likewise also the other bishops who came together signed. And those sent from Lucifer the bishop of the island of Sardinia, two deacons, Herennius and Agapetus; and from Paulinus Maximus and Calemerus, themselves also deacons. And there were present also some monks of Apollinarius the bishop, sent by him for this. And each of the aforementioned bishops is, to whom the letter was written: Eusebius of the city of Virgilli in Gaul, Lucifer of the island of Sardinia, Asterius of Petra in Arabia, Cymatius of Paltus in Coele Syria, Anatolius of Euboea. And those who sent the letter: the pope Athanasius, and those who happened to be with him in Alexandria, Eusebius himself and Asterius; and the rest: Gaius of Paratonium in nearest Libya, Agathos of Phragonis and part of Elearchia of Egypt; Ammonius of Pachnemunis and the remaining part of Elearchia, Agathodaemon of Schedia and Menelaites; Dracontius of lesser Hermopolis, Adelphius of Onuphis of Lychnon, Hermion of Tanis, Marcus of Zygri in nearest Libya, Theodore of Athribis, Andreas of Arsinoites, Paphnutius of Sais, Marcus of Philae, Zoilus of Andros, Menas of Antiphron.

choices.why: The participle is active and describes the action of defending their faith, not a static role.
The genitive absolute connects the intolerance of the unwilling confessors to the following counsel, keeping the source's causal link.
rejected: And do not tolerate such people

choices.why: The diminutive conveys the author's dismissive tone toward mere verbal disputes.

choices.english: give a neighbor a turbid overthrow to drink
choices.why: The metaphor is kept literal to preserve the image of causing another to drink something murky and destabilizing.
rejected: give their neighbor muddy water to drink

choices.why: The verb means to dictate or set down in writing, matching the context of recording the confession.
The source uses πάπας for Athanasius; rendering it as 'pope' preserves the title as given.

pass_b_english: From these things, then, they affirmed that they understand everything in the Gospel in this way, and that they hold the same mind about the incarnation and the Word's becoming human. Since these things have been confessed in this way, we urge you: do not hastily condemn those who confess and interpret the words they use in this manner, and do not reject them, but rather receive them as people making peace and making a defense. But those who are unwilling to confess and explain the words in this way, hinder them and put them to shame, as people suspected of unsound thinking. And not tolerating these, counsel also those who interpret and think rightly to examine one another no further and to quarrel over words for no useful purpose, nor to fight over such words, but to agree in the mind of godliness. For those who do not think in this way, but only contend over such little words and seek beyond what was written at Nicaea, do nothing other than give their neighbor turbid confusion to drink, as people who begrudge peace and love divisions. But you, as good people and faithful servants and stewards of the Lord, stop and hinder the things that cause scandal and astonishment, and prefer above all such peace, since the faith is sound. Perhaps the Lord will have mercy on us and join together what has been divided, and when there is one flock, we will all again have one leader, our Lord Jesus Christ. We, even though nothing more should be sought than the Council of Nicaea, nor should words from contentiousness be tolerated, nevertheless for the sake of peace and so as not to reject those who wish to believe rightly, we examined these things and briefly dictated what they confessed—we who remained in Alexandria, together with our fellow ministers Asterius and Eusebius; for most of us were away in our own districts. But you, again, in common where you are accustomed to gather, read these things, and there deem it right to call everyone. For it is right that the letter be read there first, and that those who wish and claim peace be joined there; and then, when they have been joined, wherever it pleases all the peoples, with your kindness present, let the assemblies be held there, and let the Lord be glorified in common by all. The brothers with me greet you. I pray that you fare well and remember us in the Lord. I, Athanasius; likewise the other bishops who gathered signed. And those sent from Lucifer, bishop of the island of Sardinia, were two deacons, Herennius and Agapetus; and from Paulinus, Maximus and Calemerus, also deacons. There were also present some monks of Apollinarius the bishop, sent by him for this purpose. Each of the aforementioned bishops to whom the letter was written is: Eusebius of the city of Vercelli in Gaul, Lucifer of the island of Sardinia, Asterius of Petra in Arabia, Cymatius of Paltus in Coele Syria, Anatolius of Euboea. Those who sent the letter were Pope Athanasius and those present with him in Alexandria, namely Eusebius and Asterius; and the rest: Gaius of Paratonium in nearby Libya, Agathos of Phragonis and part of Elearchia of Egypt; Ammonius of Pachnemounis and the rest of the part of Elearchia, Agathodaemon of Schedia and Menelaites; Dracontius of lesser Hermopolis, Adelphius of Onouphis of Lychnon, Hermion of Tanis, Marcus of Zygri in nearby Libya, Theodore of Athribis, Andreas of Arsinoites, Paphnutius of Sais, Marcus of Philae, Zoilus of Andros, Menas of Antiphron.

problems.quote: as people suspect in their thinking
problems.why: ὑπόπτους means 'suspected'/'suspect' (passive), not 'suspect in their thinking' (active); τῷ φρονήματι is dative of respect, 'suspect in respect of their thinking' i.e. 'suspected of unsound thinking'
problems.fix: as people suspected of unsound thinking

problems.quote: give a neighbor a turbid overthrow to drink
problems.why: ἀνατροπή here means 'draught/cup' (metaphorical), not 'overthrow'; the phrase means 'give their neighbor a turbid draught to drink'
problems.fix: give their neighbor a turbid draught to drink
problems.ruling: ἀνατροπή in this proverbial phrase means 'draught/cup,' not 'overthrow'; 'turbid overthrow' misleads readers.

problems.why: This is LXX Proverbs 3:31-32 (or related to Prov 3:31 MT 'envy the violent'), not Habakkuk 2:15; the verse about giving someone a drink to expose their nakedness is Hab 2:15 but uses different wording
problems.ruling: The quotation matches LXX Prov 3:31-32, not Hab 2:15; wrong scripture reference misleads readers.

dismissed.quote: give their neighbor turbid confusion to drink
dismissed.why: ἀνατροπὴν means 'overthrow' or 'subversion', not 'confusion'; the image is of making someone drink something that causes them to stumble/fall, not mere confusion.
